prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports (Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport) keep safety authority. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline); these reject data lacking Time Synchronization Service timestamp. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger; Alert Distribution Hub (Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter; East/West Apron Sensor; Gate Conflict Detector; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message to DPS); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Sector Load Monitor; Common Situation Display; Contingency Operations Console (recovery options with rationale, benefit, assumptions, secondary effects); Arrival Regulation Console; Post Operations Report; Airport Capacity Plan. Silverpine: emergency access after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors/decision rights: Regional Flow Manager (RFM; activate/amend/terminate flow measures); Airport Duty Manager (ADM; confirms capacity assumptions, Capacity Plan, mode changes); Tower Supervisor (ATC safety, runway sequencing); Slot Coordinator (slot fairness, compliance, exceptions); Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time) and Aircraft Operator Representative (AOR) give realistic intentions, honor agreed times; Ramp Control Lead, Ground Handling Dispatcher keep surface/handling status; Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison disclose constraints; Emergency Response Coordinator (protective measures); Deicing Coordinator (deicing constraints); Data Governance Steward (retention, consent, quality, use); System Support Engineer (24/7, advisory); Network Operations Liaison. Modes: Normal; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction; Recovery; Slot Compliance; Contingency Fallback (ADM after consulting RFM). No silent mode changes; no automatic Ground Delay Program, AAR or tactical change without authorized human confirmation. Log and Ledger record option, user response, final decision. Future releases shadow-mode validated; IAS, Time Sync, Warehouse scaled early; repeatable onboarding; cross-border exchange; explainable learning models; TOBT predictions with confidence for SAE.

New part:
S970: The Data Governance Steward is accountable for data quality rules, retention policy, access controls, and permitted operational use of shared data.
S971: The System Support Engineer is accountable for technical availability, fault response, configuration control, and coordinated restoration of the operational services.
S972: The Regional Flow Platform is the primary operational environment for the common regional plan, while the Airport CDM Portal is the primary airport coordination environment.
S973: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, and Sector Load Monitor provide planning evidence, but accountable human authorities remain responsible for operational decisions.
S974: The Common Situation Display is the shared baseline for time-critical coordination and should be kept consistent with the Regional Flow Platform and Airport CDM Portal.
S975: The Collaborative Decision Log is the authoritative record of significant decisions, objections, approvals, and operational rationale during coordinated operations.
S976: Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time commitments should be treated as executable operating constraints unless they are revised through the agreed coordination process.
S977: Ground Delay Program decisions, Tactical Regulation Proposal review, and Airport Acceptance Rate changes should be visible to affected participants before they are applied whenever operational time permits.
S978: Information-sharing duties include timely maintenance of the Flight Intent Message, Airport Capacity Plan, and other agreed planning data needed for demand and capacity balancing.
S979: The Flight Data Exchange, Airline Interface Adapter, Surface Surveillance Adapter, and Weather Ingest Gateway must be operated with monitored data quality thresholds and clear fallback procedures.
S980: The Slot Allocation Engine, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Tower Sequence Manager, and Ramp Movement Board must use the approved rules recorded in the Business Rules Registry.
S981: The Identity Access Service and Audit Event Ledger must support traceability, least-privilege access, and after-action accountability for all operationally significant changes.
S982: The Performance Analytics Warehouse and Post Operations Report should be used to measure compliance, delay outcomes, capacity use, and the effectiveness of collaborative decisions.
S983: Governance should favor transparent decision making, timely challenge by affected parties, documented resolution of disputes, and continuous improvement through training, exercises, and post-operations review.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
